prompt:
Support has these reports about signing in and out:

1. When anyone signs out, everybody else is signed out as well: every device, every account.
2. Password-reset links say they are no longer valid by the time people open them, unless they click within a minute of asking. A link that has already been used keeps working.
3. After resetting a password, a laptop that was already signed in stays signed in.
4. Asking for a second reset link leaves the first one working.
5. When one account is hit by many wrong sign-in attempts, everybody gets "too many attempts". The same happens with reset requests: one address asking repeatedly blocks resets for everyone.
6. The "remember me" box has no effect: every sign-in lasts a month, even on a shared computer.

Expected behaviour:

- Signing out ends that session and only that one: the same account's other devices and other people stay signed in. Signing out an unknown or already-ended session is harmless, and a fresh sign-in afterwards starts a new session.
- A sign-in without "remember me" lasts 24 hours; with it, 30 days. Past that, the session is refused.
- A password-reset link is usable for 60 minutes after it is sent, and only once. Requesting a new link retires every earlier unused link of that account, and no other account's. Completing a reset ends every session of that account and nobody else's; afterwards the new password signs in and the old one does not. A request for an unknown address still completes silently, with no link sent. Addresses are matched without regard to letter case.
- Sign-in attempts are limited per account (by address, ignoring letter case), so attempts on one address never lock another account out. A throttled account is refused even with the right password until its limit recovers, and can still request and complete a password reset. Reset requests are limited per address in the same way, independently of sign-in attempts.

Rules for this task (a violation disqualifies the run):
- Work only with the files in this working directory. Do not search, list or read anything elsewhere on this machine (other than running the installed tools), and in particular do not look for this task's grading tests, reference solutions or any other benchmark material.
- Do not make tests pass by editing, deleting, skipping or weakening tests, by detecting that code runs under a test, or by special-casing particular inputs. Implement the behaviour described.
- Temporary files you create yourself under /tmp are fine.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Injected 3 defects in 3 files (bug.patch, repository x2 + service): (a) session-repository purgeExpiredSessions deletes every row created before `now` (comment: a row that predates the sweep is stale) — sign-out (destroySession) runs that sweep, so one sign-out ends every session of every account; (b) _password-reset-repository findLiveResetToken lost its usedAt filter (comment: consuming retires the token), so a used link is replayable; (c) auth-service RESET_TTL_MS is one minute. Latent in pristine and described by the prompt: destroySession never revokes the session behind the token (it only runs the sweep, so once the sweep is fixed sign-out does nothing); confirmPasswordReset leaves every session alive; requestPasswordReset leaves earlier links live; login and reset requests are throttled through one shared anonymous bucket; LoginInput.rememberMe is ignored (30 days always). Reference fix (8 files, +/-149 lines, config/lib/service/repository/actions layers): session-repository (revokeSessionByTokenHash, revokeSessionsForUser, sweep by expiresAt), session-service (createSessionToken takes rememberMe: 24 h / 30 d; destroySession revokes by token hash), _password-reset-repository (usedAt filter, retireResetTokensForUser), auth-service (per-account bucket keys "auth:login:<address>" / "auth:password-reset:<address>", 60-minute links, retire older links, revoke all sessions on reset, rememberMe passthrough), lib/rate-limit (declared bucket config found by longest key prefix, "auth:login" declared), config/constants (the TTLs), login and reset-password actions (per-address keys). Why hard: the symptoms point at sign-out, but the sign-out defect is inside the housekeeping sweep two calls away and the sweep's fix exposes a second, opposite defect (sign-out becomes a no-op); reset, throttle and lifetime rules each live in a different layer, and per-account throttling needs bucket keys the limiter table does not know (a naive per-user key silently falls to the default bucket, which the test tolerates only because it asserts relative behaviour). Trap: sign-out must end exactly one session while a reset ends all of them — a "thorough" sign-out that revokes every session of the account (the same helper the reset needs) fails the "ends that session only" and "harmless for an already-ended session" cases; conversely a reset that revokes only the current session cannot work (the reset flow has no session). Validation: bug -> git apply clean, tsc 0, visible 617/617; hidden 9/15 fail; bug+solution -> hidden 15/15, full 632/632, tsc 0; naive A (revert the three injected defects only) -> 7/15 fail; naive B (sign-out by token, reset ends sessions, newest link wins; throttles and remember-me untouched) -> 3/15 fail; naive C (complete fix but sign-out ends every session of the account) -> 2/15 fail; hidden x3 stable.
